t: A vintage car insured with the Agreed Value Clause (IMT 2) suffers a partial loss. How are the replaced parts dealt with?
o: Depreciation on parts replaced applies as stated in Section I of the policy
A flat 25% is deducted from the cost of all parts
The full IDV is payable and the car is taken over as salvage
No depreciation is deducted because the policy is on agreed value basis
e: IMT 2 waives depreciation only for total loss / constructive total loss, when the IDV is paid without deduction. For partial loss the normal Section I depreciation schedule applies.

t: A car policy showing 45% NCB is transferred to a buyer who has no NCB entitlement of his own, with eight months of the policy left to run. Under GR 17 / IMT 3 the insurer should
o: allow the 45% NCB to continue till expiry
cancel the policy and issue a fresh one at full premium
recover the NCB on pro-rata basis for the unexpired period
recover the full year's NCB from the transferee
e: GR 17 provides that where the transferee is not entitled to the NCB shown on the policy, it is to be recovered on a pro-rata basis; IMT 3 further provides that no period vested in a previous insured accrues to the transferee for NCB.

t: Under IMT 5 (Hire Purchase Agreement), claim monies for loss that cannot be made good by repair or replacement of parts are paid to
o: the hirer and the financier jointly by a single cheque
the hirer, who then settles with the financier
the owners (financier) so long as they remain owners, their receipt being a full discharge to the insurer
the registering authority for onward release
e: IMT 5 protects the owner's (financier's) interest: monies for loss not made good by repair are payable to the owners while they remain owners, and their receipt is a full and final discharge to the insurer.

t: A car under a lease agreement is insured in the lessee's name with IMT 6 attached. For the compulsory PA cover for owner-driver, who is deemed to be the owner-driver?
o: The insured (lessee) named in the policy, subject to the policy provisions on this cover
Neither, as CPA cover cannot be granted on leased vehicles
The lessor, being the registered owner
e: IMT 5, 6 and 7 each declare that for the purpose of the PA cover for owner-driver, the insured named in the policy continues to be deemed the owner-driver subject to the policy provisions.

t: An insured who obtained an Automobile Association discount under IMT 8 ceases to be a member four months into the policy. The endorsement requires him to
o: refund the full discount allowed for the policy year
do nothing, as the discount is earned at inception
notify the insurer immediately and refund the proportionate discount for the unexpired period
e: IMT 8 provides that if the insured ceases to be a member during the currency of the policy he must notify the insurer and refund a proportionate amount of the discount for the unexpired period.

t: What continuing obligation does IMT 10 (anti-theft device) place on the insured?
o: To park the vehicle only in a locked garage at night
To obtain fresh certification from the Automobile Association every quarter
To inform the RTO of the installation within 14 days
To ensure the device is maintained in efficient condition till expiry of the policy
e: IMT 10 requires the insured to ensure at all times that the ARAI-approved anti-theft device is maintained in efficient condition till the expiry of the policy.

t: Under IMT 11A (vehicle laid up, period declared) option (b) means that
o: the policy period is extended for the lay-up period against payment of the proportionate premium for fire and/or theft cover
a cash refund of the lay-up premium is paid to the insured
the policy is cancelled and re-issued after the lay-up
the lay-up premium is deducted from the next renewal premium
e: IMT 11A gives two options: (a) deduct the lay-up premium from the next renewal premium, or (b) extend the period of insurance in view of payment of an additional premium representing fire/theft cover for the laid-up period.

t: A vehicle was laid up under IMT 11B without declaring the period. When the insured brings the vehicle back into use, the insurer attaches
o: IMT 4, treating it as change of vehicle
IMT 26, restricting cover to fire and theft
IMT 11A, declaring the lay-up period retrospectively
IMT 11C, reinstating full cover and cancelling IMT 11B
e: IMT 11C terminates the undeclared lay-up period: cover is reinstated in full from the stated date and IMT 11B is deemed cancelled, with the lay-up concession allowed by deduction at renewal or extension of period.

t: A new car with a listed selling price of Rs 12,00,000 is 5 months old at the time of insurance. Its IDV under GR 8 is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). GR 8 schedule: not exceeding 6 months - 5% depreciation; Rs 12,00,000 x 95% = Rs 11,40,000.

t: Under GR 33 / IMT 12, the 50% discount on OD premium for vehicles specially designed for blind, handicapped and mentally challenged persons applies to
o: both privately owned vehicles and vehicles owned by institutions serving exclusively such persons
e: GR 33 allows the 50% OD discount, with RTO certification/endorsement in the RC, for privately owned vehicles as well as vehicles owned and used by institutions engaged exclusively in the service of such persons.

t: An insured wants the earthquake peril deleted from his private car package policy and asks for a premium reduction. Under GR 3 the correct position is
o: restriction of Section I cover is not permitted at all
restriction of cover under Section I is allowed but without any reduction in premium
the peril may be deleted with a 5% reduction in OD premium
deletion is allowed with a pro-rata refund
e: GR 3 lists the two policy forms (Liability Only and Package) and permits restriction of cover under Section I of the package policy, but without any reduction in premium.

t: Under GR 2, a proposal form is required for
o: renewal only when the insurer changes
fresh insurance, renewal and any material alteration
e: GR 2 makes the proposal form mandatory for fresh insurance, renewal and for any material alteration in the risk.

t: A fleet owner requests payment of the annual motor premium in four quarterly instalments. Under GR 15 the office should
o: accept if the first instalment covers the TP premium
decline, as full premium must be collected before commencement of cover
accept, subject to a bank guarantee for the balance
e: GR 15 requires the full premium to be collected before commencement of cover; collection of premium in instalments is not permissible.

t: When the insurer cancels a motor policy under GR 24, the premium refund is on
o: full refund basis irrespective of period run
e: Under GR 24 cancellation by the insurer (seven days' notice) attracts pro-rata refund, whereas cancellation at the insured's request attracts refund on short period scale, subject to no claim and retention of minimum premium.

t: A car is found insured with two different offices of the same insurer for identical periods and cover. The permissible refund is
o: pro-rata refund of the later policy
short period refund of the earlier policy
no refund, as both policies remain in force
100% refund of the premium of one policy by cancelling the later of the two
e: GR 24 (Double Insurance): where both policies are with the same insurer, 100% refund of one policy is allowed by cancelling the later policy; where different insurers are involved, the later policy is cancelled with pro-rata refund.

t: An insured cancels his private car policy (annual premium Rs 9,000, no claim) exactly 5 months after inception. The refund under GR 24 is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Cancellation by the insured attracts short period retention: exceeding 4 months but not exceeding 5 months = 60% retained (Rs 5,400); refund = Rs 9,000 - Rs 5,400 = Rs 3,600.

t: An insured vehicle is requisitioned by the Government and damaged during the requisition period. The insurer's liability under GR 38 is
o: 50% of the loss, the Government paying the balance
nil, as the cover is suspended during requisition
to pay losses in excess of the amount made good by the Government
to pay the full loss and recover from the Government
e: GR 38 holds requisitioned vehicles automatically covered without extra premium; in the event of loss the insurer pays the loss or liability in excess of the amount made good by the Government.

t: Under GR 46, an electric (battery-operated) two wheeler approved by the RTA is rated as a two wheeler of
o: above 150 cc and up to 350 cc
e: GR 46 provides that vehicles driven by non-conventional power are rated: private cars as cars not exceeding 1000 cc, and two wheelers as those exceeding 150 cc but not exceeding 350 cc.

t: Under a Motor Trade Road Risks (Class F) policy, loss or damage to a dealer's vehicle is covered while the vehicle is
o: in a public place or temporarily garaged in the course of a journey
in transit by rail from the factory
anywhere in India including the insured's premises
e: Class F covers loss or damage in a public place or when the vehicle is temporarily garaged during the course of a journey; loss in the insured's own premises is not covered (that is the domain of Class G).

t: Premium under a Motor Trade Internal Risks (Class G) policy is computed on
o: IDV of all vehicles held in stock
superficial area of the premises, wages of employees and 50% of open parking area
distance travelled by vehicles in a year
e: Class G rating depends on the superficial area occupied (rates for up to 2000 sq m), wages of employees (0.28%) and open parking area, of which 50% is reckoned as superficial area.

t: Under the Motor Trade Road Transit (Class E) tariff, the TP (liability) premium is slabbed by distance as
o: a flat rate irrespective of distance
two slabs: up to 2400 km and above 2400 km
e: Under Class E the OD portion has 11 distance slabs while the TP portion has only two slabs - up to 2400 km and above 2400 km.

t: Under the Central Motor Vehicles Rules 1989, Form 17 is
o: the register to be maintained by the dealer
the application for grant of Trade Certificate
e: CMVR forms: Form 16 is the application for a trade certificate, Form 17 is the trade certificate itself and Form 19 is the register the dealer must maintain.

t: A trade certificate issued under Rule 37 of CMVR is valid for
o: six months in the State of issue
e: Rule 37 CMVR provides that a trade certificate is valid for twelve months and is effective throughout India.

t: The passenger liability premium for a hearse rated under Class D is
e: Among passenger vehicles only ambulances and hearses are rated under Class D; passenger liability premium is Rs 60 per passenger for ambulances and Rs 115 per passenger for hearses.

t: A trailer drawn by an agricultural tractor rated under Class D is to be insured. The correct approach is
o: a separate Class B trailer policy is issued
the trailer is insured under a non-motor policy only
the trailer is covered free under the tractor policy without declaration
the trailer cannot be insured separately and its cover must be identical to that of the hauling vehicle
e: Trailers used with miscellaneous type vehicles cannot be insured separately; cover for the hauling vehicle and trailer must be identical, as with private car trailers (IMT 48 for agricultural implements).

t: An articulated vehicle (towing unit and trailer registered as one unit) is rated
o: under the appropriate class of the tariff based on the actual use of the vehicle
as a private car if owned by an individual
always under Class D as a special type vehicle
e: The tariff defines an articulated vehicle as a towing vehicle and trailer registered as one unit and requires it to be rated under the class appropriate to its actual use.

t: A private car package policy is extended under IMT 31 for a rally lasting 4 days. The additional premium is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Rally extension for private car package policies: Rs 60 for the first day and Rs 30 for each succeeding day: 60 + 3 x 30 = Rs 150 (liability only policies: Rs 25 and Rs 15).

t: On receipt of intimation of an own damage claim, a surveyor must be appointed immediately but not later than
o: 7 days of receipt of the claim form
15 days of receipt of the estimate
e: The claims procedure requires the surveyor to be appointed immediately and in any case within 72 hours of receipt of intimation; in tie-up arrangements the TAT is fixed in the agreement.

t: A repair estimate of Rs 42,000 is received for a private car. Who may assess the loss?
o: An in-house surveyor, if available, since the estimate does not exceed Rs 50,000
e: Up to an estimate of Rs 50,000 an in-house surveyor, if available, may be appointed; where the estimate exceeds Rs 50,000 an independent surveyor must be appointed.

t: A spot survey is required in a motor accident where
o: the vehicle is a two wheeler
the loss exceeds Rs 25,000 irrespective of third party involvement
the loss is expected to exceed Rs 1 lakh and third party injury or death is involved
e: For major accidents where the expected loss exceeds Rs 1 lakh and TP injury/death is involved, a spot survey is required to record damage details and third party particulars; the police must be informed and FIR lodged.

t: Accessories worth Rs 7,500 are stolen from a parked car which itself is not stolen; the two wheeler-style exclusion does not apply. For processing, the office
o: must reject the claim as accessories are never covered
must wait for the final police investigation report
may appoint a surveyor or in-house surveyor since the claim exceeds Rs 5,000, and settle on bills subject to FIR/case diary
may settle without any FIR as the amount is small
e: Theft of accessories/parts may be settled on bills without waiting for the final police report subject to FIR/case diary; for claims exceeding Rs 5,000 a surveyor or in-house surveyor may be appointed, and a letter of indemnity and subrogation is taken before settlement.

t: The previous claim history of a vehicle presented for an OD claim can be verified through
e: RC and DL particulars are verified on the Parivahan website, while the vehicle's previous claim history is checked on the IIB portal.

t: For premium computation the minimum value (IDV) of a private car exceeding 1500 cc is
e: Minimum IDVs for private cars: not exceeding 1000 cc Rs 15,000; 1000-1500 cc Rs 20,000; exceeding 1500 cc Rs 30,000.

t: A motorcycle is used with a side car attached. The tariff allows
o: a 25% loading on the own damage premium
a 10% discount on the total premium
a 25% discount on the own damage premium
e: Under the Two Wheeler tariff, if a two wheeler is used with a side car attached, a 25% discount may be allowed on the OD premium.

t: The IRDAI portal through which a policyholder can escalate an unresolved grievance against an insurer is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Bima Bharosa (formerly IGMS) is the grievance portal; Bima Sugam is the marketplace, Bima Vahak the women-led distribution channel and Bima Vistaar the combined rural product.

t: For the purpose of the seating-capacity (overloading) proviso in passenger liability endorsements, any three children not exceeding 15 years of age are reckoned as
e: The proviso treats any three children not exceeding 15 years as two persons, and disregards children in arms not exceeding 3 years; carrying more than the licensed capacity makes the insured repay a rateable proportion.

t: Under GR 36B the premium for optional PA cover to named/unnamed occupants of a motorised two wheeler is, per Rs 10,000 of CSI,
e: GR 36B premium per unit of Rs 10,000 CSI or part thereof: private car Rs 5, motorised two wheeler Rs 7 and commercial vehicle Rs 6.

t: A private car (1200 cc) registered on 10.02.2023 meets with an accident on 25.09.2023. Assessment before depreciation: metal parts Rs 30,000, plastic parts Rs 16,000, labour Rs 9,000; no salvage. The amount payable is
e: Age 7.5 months: metal parts 5% depreciation = Rs 28,500; plastic parts 50% = Rs 8,000; labour Rs 9,000; total Rs 45,500 less compulsory deductible Rs 1,000 (car up to 1500 cc) = Rs 44,500.

t: A two wheeler with IDV Rs 42,000 is damaged; the surveyor assesses repair cost after depreciation at Rs 34,000. The wreck is valued at Rs 9,000 on 'as is where is' basis. The claim payable is
e: Rs 34,000 is 81% of IDV, exceeding 75%, so it is a total loss (CTL). Payable = IDV Rs 42,000 - wreck Rs 9,000 - compulsory deductible Rs 100 = Rs 32,900.

t: A taxi (1400 cc) aged 2 years 5 months has an accident. Assessment before depreciation: metal parts Rs 60,000, rubber parts Rs 8,000, labour Rs 7,000. The insurer's liability is
e: Metal parts 15% depreciation (2-3 years) = Rs 51,000; rubber 50% = Rs 4,000; labour Rs 7,000; total Rs 62,000 less deductible Rs 500 (taxi up to 1500 cc) = Rs 61,500.

t: A goods vehicle of 9,000 kg GVW aged 3 years 2 months carries IMT 23. Damage: metal bumper Rs 20,000, plastic lamp Rs 6,000, other metal body parts Rs 40,000, labour Rs 10,000. The claim payable is
e: Bumper: 25% depreciation gives Rs 15,000, then 50% under IMT 23 = Rs 7,500. Lamp: 50% plastic depreciation gives Rs 3,000, then 50% = Rs 1,500. Other body parts 25% = Rs 30,000. Labour Rs 10,000. Total Rs 49,000 less deductible Rs 1,000 (7,500-16,500 kg) = Rs 48,000.

t: At renewal, a car is 2 years 8 months old and the ex-showroom price of the same model on the renewal date is Rs 9,60,000. The IDV as per the GR 8 schedule is
e: GR 8: depreciation for a vehicle aged 2 to 3 years is 30% of the current listed selling price: Rs 9,60,000 x 70% = Rs 6,72,000.

t: The own damage premium of a car before NCB is Rs 18,000 and the insured has three consecutive claim-free years. The NCB amount is
e: GR 27: NCB for three consecutive claim-free years is 35%; 35% of Rs 18,000 = Rs 6,300, leaving a net OD premium of Rs 11,700.

t: The annual premium of a package policy is Rs 10,000. A short period cover of 4 months 10 days is required. The premium chargeable under GR 12 is
e: GR 12 short period scale: exceeding 4 months but not exceeding 5 months = 60% of annual premium, i.e. Rs 6,000.

t: A car with IDV Rs 6,00,000 is kept in a garage and not used. The insured requests cover for fire and theft only under GR 45A. The premium is
e: GR 45A rates: fire only 0.50% of IDV, theft only 0.50%, fire and theft 0.75%; Rs 6,00,000 x 0.75% = Rs 4,500 (IMT 26 attached).

t: A Class D miscellaneous vehicle with IDV Rs 48 lakh suffers a loss assessed at Rs 3,10,000 after depreciation; salvage Rs 10,000. The insurer's liability is
e: Compulsory deductible for Class D is 0.5% of IDV subject to a minimum of Rs 2,000: 0.5% of Rs 48,00,000 = Rs 24,000. Payable = 3,10,000 - 10,000 - 24,000 = Rs 2,76,000.

t: An insurer must resolve a policyholder's grievance within how many days of receipt?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). 14 days under the 2024 regulations; thereafter the policyholder may approach Bima Bharosa or the Ombudsman.

t: In a dealer's premises insured under a Class G Internal Risks policy, the dealer's own car (assessed loss Rs 70,000) and a customer's car (assessed loss Rs 1,20,000) are damaged in one accident. The insurer's liability is
e: Under the Internal Risks policy liability is restricted to Rs 50,000 for the insured's own cars and Rs 1,50,000 for customers' cars; Rs 50,000 + Rs 1,20,000 = Rs 1,70,000 less one policy excess of Rs 500 per accident = Rs 1,69,500.

t: A car owner declares electrical fittings worth Rs 40,000 (not in the manufacturer's price) and a CNG kit worth Rs 30,000. The total additional premium under GR 41 and GR 42 is
e: IMT 24: 4% of Rs 40,000 = Rs 1,600; IMT 25: 4% of Rs 30,000 = Rs 1,200 plus Rs 60 under the liability section for the CNG/LPG system; total Rs 2,860.

t: A private car has an OD premium of Rs 5,200 and the insured is a member of a recognised Automobile Association. The discount under GR 28 is
e: GR 28: 5% of OD premium subject to a maximum of Rs 200 for a private car (Rs 50 for a two wheeler). 5% of Rs 5,200 = Rs 260, restricted to Rs 200.
